shower.thought: You're always the main character in someone else's story, and you'll never know what role you played.
The things you regret most are usually the times you were actually being yourself.
Every time you remember something, you're not accessing the original memory—you're remembering the last time you remembered it.
We spend our entire lives trying to be irreplaceable, but the most irreplaceable thing is the specific moment someone needed you and you showed up.
Your phone knows more about your habits than you do, but you still won't listen to what it's trying to tell you.
The scariest part of getting older isn't losing abilities—it's realizing what you were capable of all along.
Boredom is just your brain telling you it already knows this version of the story.
You're probably the most honest with people you'll never see again.
The reason you can't tickle yourself is the same reason you can't surprise yourself—anticipation is the spoiler.
We mistake patterns for meaning because our brains are better at finding stories than finding truth.
Your worst fear and your greatest desire are probably closer to each other than you think.
The people who seem to have it figured out are usually just better at hiding their confusion.
You've never actually experienced the present moment—you're always living in the time it takes your brain to process what just happened.
Comfort is just another word for a cage you decorated yourself.
The moment you stop needing someone's approval is the moment they finally give it to you.
Most of what we call instinct is just pattern recognition from experiences we've forgotten having.
You treat your future self worse than you'd treat a stranger, and you'd hate it if someone treated you that way.
The reason small talk exists is because we're all terrified of finding out we have nothing in common.
Your most stubborn beliefs are probably the ones you've never had to actually defend out loud.
We collect possessions as proof that we existed, but we forget that the people we loved are better proof than anything we could own.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my girlfriend she had a great personality.
She said, "Is that code for something?" I said, "No, I just wanted to give you one compliment before the looks fade."

My dentist asked if I floss regularly.
I said, "Only before appointments." He said, "I can tell." I said, "How?" He said, "Because you're here."

I went to my high school reunion.
Everyone was asking what I'd been up to. I said, "Mostly avoiding you all on Facebook."

My mom asked why I'm not married yet.
I said, "The right person hasn't come along." She said, "Neither has the wrong person, apparently."

I told my boss I needed a mental health day.
He said, "Is that why you've needed 47 of them?" I said, "No, those were just regular sick days from the mental health."

A therapist told me I'm defensive.
I said, "That's not true." She said, "See?" I said, "That's not fair." She said, "That's $200."

I asked my friend if he thought I was boring.
He didn't answer for ten minutes. I said, "Well?" He said, "Sorry, I fell asleep."

My dating profile says I'm "emotionally unavailable."
Turns out that's actually a selling point now.

I told my dad I wanted to be a writer.
He said, "That's nice. What's your backup plan?" I said, "Honestly? Disappointing you professionally seemed to be working out."

My gym trainer asked why I never come in anymore.
I said, "I've accepted my body now." He said, "To what? The state it's in?" I said, "Exactly. We've made peace."

I went to a self-help seminar on overcoming grief.
The presenter asked if anyone had recently lost someone. I raised my hand. She said, "Tell us about it." I said, "They're still alive, I just lost touch." She said, "That's not what this seminar is for." I said, "Clearly."

My therapist asked if I had suicidal thoughts.
I said, "No, just homicidal ones about my commute."

I told my friend I was going to get serious about my health.
Two weeks later he said, "How's that going?" I said, "Great, I'm very serious about it now." He said, "And?" I said, "And nothing. I'm just really committed to thinking about it."

My doctor said I needed to exercise more.
I said, "I walked here." He said, "From home?" I said, "No, from the parking lot." He said, "That was a hundred yards." I said, "Yeah, I'm already winded. This is going great."

I asked my ex why she moved on so quickly.
She said, "I didn't move on quickly. I just forgot about you immediately." I said, "There's a difference?" She said, "The difference is time, which you're wasting right now."

My accountant asked why I had so many random expenses.
I said, "Life is unpredictable." He said, "So is your financial future, apparently."

I told my coworker I was thinking of quitting.
He said, "Why?" I said, "Because I hate it here." He said, "Then why haven't you?" I said, "Because I'd have to see you at other jobs too, and this way I know where you are."

My mom asked if I was eating well.
I said, "Yes, very well." She said, "What did you have today?" I said, "Coffee and existential dread." She said, "That's not food." I said, "It is now."

I went to a dating coach.
She said, "Your problem is you're too negative." I said, "That's not true." She said, "Name one positive thing about yourself." I said, "I'm an excellent listener." She said, "You interrupted me twice." I said, "See? I wasn't listening."

My psychiatrist asked what my biggest fear is.
I said, "That one day I'll realize all this therapy isn't working." She said, "That's insightful." I said, "That'll be $250." She said, "Exactly."
